title: autotune: default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ CLI tooling
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token serving cost by providing sensible defaults and automation for batching, prefix/KV caching, and model quantization profiles, and expose unit-economics tooling to make tradeoffs observable and actionable. This PR implements: 1) autotune defaults for batching and caching surfaced in the serving config; 2) a set of validated quantization profiles (INT8/4-bit heuristics + fallbacks) for common model families in the model registry; 3) a new 'redwood uecon' CLI that computes expected per-request cost given workload traces and suggests configuration deltas. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-9421) - [x] Runtime changes: batching/caching heuristics - [x] Model registry: quant profiles + compatibility matrix - [x] CLI: unit-econ report and recommendations - [x] E2E tests and perf canary - [x] Docs + console hints - [x] Feature flags behind autoplay/autotune toggle Rollout plan: feature gated behind "autotune_defaults" flag. Start with internal canary on dedicated clusters, then gradual rollout to hosted for low-risk tenants. Reverts: clear rollback hooks added to runtime (disable autotune_defaults -> previous config restored). Full description of changes below.

release_notes: Defaults: enable autotuned batching/caching heuristics (feature-flagged); Added quantization profiles for rw-7b/rw-14b; New CLI 'redwood uecon' to estimate and recommend per-request cost; No breaking changes; Tenant-level KV cache opt-out and TTL configs.
testing_instructions: 1) Toggle feature flag 'autotune_defaults' in internal config and restart runtime on canary cluster. 2) Run perf canary: scripts/perf/run_canary.sh --suite=autotune --model=rw-7b --trace=traces/sample_workload.json. 3) Use CLI: 'redwood uecon estimate --trace traces/sample_workload.json --model rw-7b' to validate unit-econ numbers. 4) Verify KV cache metrics in /metrics and console (cache_hit_ratio > 0.2 for prefix-heavy workloads).
impact_assessment: Benchmarks show median token cost reduction of ~22% on rw-7b in prefix-heavy workloads and ~12% on rw-14b with INT8 profiles; p50 latency improved by 8-15% depending on workload. Tail latency (p99) unchanged after conservative autotuner adjustments. Expected platform-level savings: estimated $0.08-$0.15 per 1k tokens served for typical PLG workloads that are caching-friendly.
perf_results: Canary run (internal): rw-7b prefix-heavy: p50 latency 42ms (baseline 46ms), p95 110ms (baseline 126ms), p99 240ms (baseline 238ms); token cost -22% with INT8 profile + caching. rw-14b mixed workload: p50 78ms (baseline 85ms), p95 210ms (baseline 230), token cost -12% with 4-bit profile.
notes: Model registry quant profiles include fallbacks to fp16 when performance regressions detected during warmup. All autotune behavior is controllable per-tenant and exposed in the console as recommendations before applying live changes.
change_risks: Medium: runtime autotuning can interact with tenant SLAs; mitigations include per-tenant opt-outs, conservative defaults, gradual rollout, and automatic rollback triggers when p99 latency increases >10%.
